facts.raw_span: decreased vision in her right eye
Symptoms began 4 days prior to presentation
struck by lightning directly to the right forehead
Uncorrected visual acuity measured 20/50 OD and 20/20 OS
Pupils were symmetric, with no relative afferent pupillary defect
Initial anterior segment examination was normal with absence of cataract
Initial dilated fundus examination showed no apparent abnormalities in either eye
central macular thickening in fundus examination at 2 weeks
mild posterior subcapsular cataract visible in right eye at 7 weeks
Intraretinal cystoid changes and subfoveal ellipsoid zone disruption in the right eye at two weeks post-injury
Restoration of foveal contour with decreased cystoid abnormalities, small subfoveal hyporeflective space, and further loss of outer retinal layers in the nasal macula at seven weeks post-injury
Persistent subfoveal hyporeflective space in the inner retina with interval restoration of subfoveal outer retinal structures at four months post-injury

concepts.why: The patient was struck by lightning and later developed a posterior subcapsular cataract, which is a known complication of electrical injury.
The patient was struck by lightning and later developed central macular thickening and intraretinal cystoid changes, which are consistent with lightning-induced maculopathy.
The patient suffered a traumatic injury from the lightning strike, which can cause cataract formation.
The patient developed central macular thickening and intraretinal cystoid changes, which are characteristic of macular edema.
The patient suffered retinal damage from the lightning strike, which caused intraretinal cystoid changes and subfoveal ellipsoid zone disruption.
The patient developed a posterior subcapsular cataract, which is a specific type of cataract that can occur after trauma or injury.
It explains the persistent subfoveal hyporeflective space in the inner retina found in the patient's eye at four months post-injury.

rationales.F01: Decreased vision in one eye suggests a localized problem, which could be related to lightning-induced maculopathy or retinal damage.
rationales.F03: Being struck by lightning directly to the forehead is a strong indicator of lightning-induced cataract, maculopathy, or retinal damage.
rationales.F08: Central macular thickening is a common finding in macular edema, which could be related to lightning-induced maculopathy.
rationales.F09: Mild posterior subcapsular cataract is a common finding in lightning-induced cataract and traumatic cataract.
rationales.F10: Intraretinal cystoid changes and subfoveal ellipsoid zone disruption are characteristic of macular edema and retinal damage, which could be related to lightning-induced maculopathy.
rationales.F12: Persistent subfoveal hyporeflective space is a characteristic finding of solitary hyporeflective inner retinal spot.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's decreased vision, central macular thickening, and intraretinal cystoid changes are best explained by Lightning-Induced Maculopathy, which is directly related to the lightning strike and supports the specific findings of macular damage.
